evidence.summary: run(x) != reference(x) on CUDA at both N=64 and N=128: single-coefficient unit rows mismatch (2368/64-matrix positions at N=64, 9472 at N=128), random and extreme (all-3328) rows mismatch, and even constant rows mismatch every position. The claim (run differs from reference for non-constant canonical rows at one or both widths) is confirmed; the constant-row failures additionally indicate the defect is broader than twiddle placement (likely indexing/reduction/wrap semantics).

rationale: The five coefficient banks (first/second/upper/cross_low/cross_high) with exponents omega^(j*width/(2*half)), omega^(j*width/(4*half)), omega^((j+half)*width/(4*half)) and the quadrant formulas lower_sum/lower_difference/upper_sum/upper_difference involve four independently chosen twiddle placements; an exponent-sign or permutation error in any of them would produce wrong outputs on any non-constant canonical input while constant rows still pass.

scope_evidence.summary: out[b,k] = sum_j x[b,j]*omega_N^(j*k) mod 3329 must hold exactly (tolerance 0/0) for EVERY canonical field value input; any twiddle exponent or quadrant permutation error violates this for non-constant rows.

scope_rationale: The contract requires exact equality (abs/rel tolerance 0) with the cyclic DFT for every canonical input, so any twiddle placement or quadrant assignment error in lines 72-83 is a contract violation on non-constant rows (constant rows can pass even with wrong twiddles).
statement: The fused radix-4 butterfly (lines 62-83) mis-assigns twiddle coefficients or quadrants, so run(x) differs from reference(x) for some non-constant canonical row (e.g. a single nonzero coefficient x[b,j]=1) at one or both of N=64 and N=128.

data.expected_signal: host-replicated _multiply arithmetic yields exact residues for all canonical value x Montgomery-coefficient products, with reduced < 2*Q so one conditional subtract suffices

evidence.summary: Exhaustive host replication of _multiply over all 3329 canonical values x all 3329 possible Montgomery-form coefficients: 0 bad results, max product 11075584 (fits int64/int32 easily), max reduced before subtract 3494 < 2*3329 so one conditional subtract always suffices, max result 3328 (canonical range). The Montgomery reduction arithmetic itself is exact; the observed output mismatch stems from another defect (see c1/c3 evidence).

rationale: The lazy Montgomery reduction (correction=(product*3327)&0xFFFF, reduced=(product+correction*3329)>>16, one conditional subtract) must produce an exact residue in [0,3328] for products up to ~3328*3328*2^16; the conditional subtract handles at most one extra 3329, and int32 re-cast truncation would also be a failure mode if the range assumptions are off.

scope_evidence.summary: Exact integer result required (absolute and relative tolerance 0) with canonical representative in [0,3328]; contract permits any internal residue representation only if the final output still equals the mathematical target exactly.

scope_rationale: The contract allows any modular-reduction algorithm but requires exact canonical results (tolerance 0/0) for all values in 0..3328, so a reduction that is off by 3329 or wraps int32 for any value/coefficient combination is a violation.
statement: The Montgomery-style reduction in _multiply (lines 41-45) is inexact for some canonical value x Montgomery-coefficient product in range, e.g. reduced can land in [3329, 6658) after a single conditional subtract fails, or the int64 intermediate overflows, producing outputs off by a multiple of 3329 or out of [0,3328].

data.expected_signal: whether last-stage offset matches and whether N=128 output equals reference or a permuted/scaled variant
data.stdout: {"offset_ok": true, "stage_offsets_ok": true, "last_start": 105, "fused_len": 105, "N128_all_ok": false, "N128_total_mismatches": 13568, "constant_row_ok": false, "constant_row_mismatches": 127, "constant_expected": 1489, "constant_out_sample": [3291, 2837, 912, 886], "unit_row0_expected": 1, "unit_row0_out_sample": [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1], "unit_row0_ok": true, "bitrev_perm_match": true, "diffs_multiple_of_3329": true}

evidence.summary: For N=128: the last-stage start offset (105) and all fused-stage bank offsets correctly match _make_coefficients' layout, and a unit impulse at j=0 is exact. However run(x) != reference(x) on 13568 of 16256 tested positions; the kernel output equals the bit-reversal permutation of the reference (bitrev_perm_match=true), i.e. the final radix-2 stage/gather produces non-natural-order output. Constant rows also fail (127/128 positions), showing an additional arithmetic defect beyond ordering. The c3 claim (last stage / natural-order path is wrong so run != reference for N=128) is confirmed.

rationale: The last-stage start offset 5*((1<<(2*(LOG_N//2)))-1)//3 must equal the fused stages' cumulative length 5*(1+4+16)=105 for N=128 (LOG_N=7 -> 5*((1<<6)-1)//3 = 105), and the bit-reversal permutation plus final gather must produce natural-order output; any mismatch affects only N=128, which N=64 evidence cannot cover.

scope_evidence.summary: N is either 64 or 128 and every canonical input at both widths is in the public domain; output position k must be frequency k in natural order. A width-specific failure at N=128 violates the contract.

scope_rationale: Both N=64 and N=128 are in the contract's public domain with natural-order output required, so a bug appearing only in the N=128 last stage or in natural-order indexing is a direct contract violation.
statement: The odd-LOG_N last stage (lines 86-95) is wrong: either the coefficient bank start offset 'start = 5*((1<<(2*(LOG_N//2)))-1)//3' does not match _make_coefficients' layout for N=128, or the final radix-2 butterfly/gather produces non-natural-order output, so run(x) != reference(x) for N=128 inputs even when N=64 passes.
